target_customer: Offices, hotels and restaurants that want specialty coffee and tea without staffing a cafe
problem: Office coffee is either low quality or needs staff and barista equipment, and pod systems waste plastic and metal.
business_model: Hardware brewer service with recurring packets of whole bean coffee, including installation, upkeep and automatic restocking
product_category: Food service machines, office coffee, IoT hardware

founders.name: Greg Kress
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an experienced founder, hardware engineer, product designer and rapid prototyping specialist.

founders.name: Scott Steber
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page, no bio given. Technical flag inferred from the CTO title only.

technical_complexity.rationale: A networked single serve brewer with packet handling needs mechanical design, food safe parts and service logistics, but the founders had hardware prototyping skills per the YC page.

defensibility.rationale: Roaster partnerships and a packet format are copyable, and no patents or exclusive contracts are cited.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says what incumbents did against Pearl. Keurig and other office coffee suppliers already served the same offices.

market_need_then: The YC description and company pages claim demand for café quality coffee in offices with no plastic pods. No spend figures, pilots or revenue were found.

branding.domain_note: Used getpearlcoffee.com, a prefix style domain, not pearl.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline from the directory: Keurig convenience meets cafe quality

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no press about the brand, and the name is shared with many other coffee businesses.

outcome_analysis: Pearl joined YC in Winter 2017 with a button press office brewer that used compostable whole bean packets from artisan roasters. The directory lists it as inactive, and the YC page labels both founders as former, but no shutdown report, post mortem or customer data was found, so the cause is not public. Failure factors are left empty for that reason.
notes: getpearlcoffee.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch, so the site is unreachable or dead. Two dated competitor searches found nothing near the batch, so the list is empty. The 120000 seed rests on a single aggregator (village.ai, an entity listed as Mere Coffee Inc) and is the standard YC amount. Directory status is Inactive; exit type unknown because no source gives the end of operations.
